meta.purpose: Data for a PC replace-vs-upgrade judgement app (mottainai).
meta.honesty_policy: No number in this file is invented. Every benchmark figure is taken verbatim from the PassMark public dataset. Fields that could not be obtained are null and carry a note containing 未取得.
known_limitations: release_year on cpus[] and gpus[] is an editorial generation mapping, NOT scraped from a source. It is flagged per-record via release_year_note. Treat as approximate.
passmark_test_date is PassMark's benchmark submission date, NOT the product launch date. Do not display it as a release date.

PassMark does not publish memSize (VRAM) for every entry. Where absent, vram_mb is null with a 未取得 note - this affects most integrated GPUs (correct, they have no dedicated VRAM) and some discrete cards.

win11_supported on cpus[] is derived by applying the Microsoft list rule (Intel Core 8th gen+, AMD Ryzen 2000 series+ excluding the 2200G/2400G Raven Ridge APUs), not by a per-model lookup against the Microsoft page.
Radeon RX 570 has no clean matching entry in the PassMark mega-page dataset and is therefore absent from gpus[].

intel.rule: Intel Core 8th generation (Coffee Lake / Kaby Lake-R) and newer are on the official list. 7th generation and older Core i3/i5/i7 are NOT listed.
families_on_list_observed: Xeon W / Xeon E / Xeon D / Xeon Scalable 1st-5th Gen / Xeon 6
intel.caveat: Some non-Core families on the list (e.g. Celeron 3000 series) predate 8th-gen Core, so "8th gen or newer" is a rule of thumb for Core-branded chips only, not a universal cutoff.

amd.rule: AMD Ryzen 2000-series desktop CPUs (2300X / 2500X / 2600 / 2600X / 2700 / 2700X) and newer are on the official list. Ryzen 1000 series (1200/1400/1600/1700/1800X) is NOT on the list.
amd.important_exception: Ryzen 3 2200G and Ryzen 5 2400G (Raven Ridge APUs) are NOT present on the Microsoft list even though their model numbers start with 2. They are Zen (1st gen) silicon. This is a common trap: a "Ryzen 2000" number does not automatically mean supported.
amd.exception_evidence: The fetched 24H2 AMD list contains Ryzen 3 2300X, Ryzen 5 2500X, Ryzen 5 2600/2600E/2600X, Ryzen 5 PRO 2600, Ryzen 7 2700/2700E/2700X, Ryzen 7 PRO 2700/2700X. It does not contain 2200G or 2400G.
families_on_list_observed: Ryzen 3/5/7/9 (2000 series and newer) incl. PRO

qualcomm.rule: Only 18 Qualcomm/Snapdragon parts are listed. The oldest Snapdragon-branded entries are Snapdragon 7c+ Gen 3 and Snapdragon 8cx Gen 2. Original Snapdragon 8cx (Gen 1) is NOT on the list.
qualcomm.note: ARM Windows machines are rare in the Japanese second-hand market, so this list matters far less than the Intel/AMD boundaries for a replace-vs-upgrade decision.

tpm_secureboot_fixable_in_bios.summary: Many PCs that fail the Windows 11 check actually HAVE a firmware TPM that is simply switched off in BIOS/UEFI. Turning it on can flip a machine from "unsupported" to "supported" with zero spend.
tpm_secureboot_fixable_in_bios.secure_boot_note: Secure Boot also requires the disk to be GPT/UEFI, not legacy MBR/CSM. Windows includes MBR2GPT to convert without reinstalling; switching CSM off before converting will make the PC fail to boot.
tpm_secureboot_fixable_in_bios.caveat: Setting names and menu locations vary by motherboard vendor; these are the common labels reported across vendor guides, not a single official Microsoft list.

ssd_vs_hdd.metric: time to usable desktop incl. startup apps, seconds
ssd_vs_hdd.note: Until all resident apps (Discord etc.) finished loading. HDD 4min vs SSD 30s = 1/8. Closest to lived experience but loosely controlled.

ssd_vs_hdd.metric: relative boot delay vs fastest NVMe, seconds
ssd_vs_hdd.note: KEY FINDING for advice logic: HDD lags the fastest NVMe by ~20s and lags SATA SSD by ~17s. PCIe4.0 vs PCIe3.0 NVMe differ by fractions of a second. SATA SSD lags NVMe by only ~1s. Therefore HDD->SSD is transformative; SATA SSD->NVMe is imperceptible for boot.

market_notes.claim: DDR4 alone keeps climbing while DDR5 is falling. DDR4-3200 16GBx2 rose 1,000 to 30,980; DDR4-3200 SO-DIMM 16GBx2 rose 3,500 to 36,300. Meanwhile DDR5-5600 16GBx2 dropped 20,000 to 39,980, the cheapest of 2026. Survey window 2026-07-25 to 08-01.

'Just add RAM' no longer holds as cheap advice. A DDR4 16GBx2 kit (30,980) costs about the same as a used Windows 11 laptop (29,800). A DDR4 SO-DIMM 32GB kit (36,300) approaches a brand-new entry laptop (43,956).
market_notes.note: This is a cross-source inference by the research agent, not a quote. The underlying unit prices are from the cited retail sources.
